questions: If there are multiple ways to make all 1s contiguous with the same minimal number of swaps, does the choice of which 1s end up in the final contiguous block matter for the count, or is the minimal number always uniquely determined regardless of which 1s are moved together?
Are adjacent swaps allowed to wrap around the ends of the string (i.e., swapping the Nth and 1st characters)?
If the string contains no '1's, is the condition 'all 1s are contiguous' considered true (vacuously) or false?
Does the operation cost count per swap, or per chosen i (i.e., swapping the same pair multiple times counts multiple times)?

If there are multiple contiguous groups of 1s initially, must the final contiguous block contain exactly the same set of 1s (i.e., no creation or deletion of 1s), or can we also change characters from 0 to 1 or vice versa?
Should the output be the minimal number of swaps, or the minimal number of operations (where each operation is a swap) as stated?
If the string has all 1s contiguous but not necessarily in a single block (e.g., '111' is contiguous, but '101' is not), does the clarification cover cases where there are no 1s?
